questions.q: What did the adversary provoke David to do?
questions.a: The adversary provoked David to count the people of Israel so that he could know the size of his army.

questions.q: How did Joab respond to David’s request to count the people?
questions.a: He resisted David and suggested that it would bring guilt on Israel.

questions.q: What did Joab do when the king commanded him to go and count the people?
questions.a: He went and counted them then reported back the total number of men that were able to fight.

questions.q: Which two tribes did Joab not include when he counted the people?
questions.a: Joab did not count Levi and Benjamin, because the king’s command displeased him.

questions.q: How did God respond to David counting the soldiers of Israel?
questions.a: God was offended and punished Israel.

questions.q: How did David respond when God punished Israel?
questions.a: He confessed his sin and asked God to forgive him.

questions.q: In response to David’s confession, what did Yahweh offer him?
What were the three choices Yahweh gave to David?
questions.a: David could choose three years of famine, three months of his enemies defeating his army, or three days of a plague sent by Yahweh.

questions.q: Which of the three punishments did David choose?
questions.a: He chose to be punished by Yahweh with a plague, because Yahweh is very merciful.

questions.q: What were the results of David’s choice?
questions.a: Yahweh sent the plague and many people died. Yahweh sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem, but Yahweh changed his mind.

questions.q: When David saw the angel with the sword, how did he react?
questions.a: He confessed and requested that God punish him and his family, but not punish God’s people.

questions.q: What was David commanded to do at the threshing floor of Ornan?
questions.a: David was commanded to build an altar to Yahweh at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

questions.q: How did Ornan react to seeing the angel?
questions.a: He and his four sons hid themselves from the angel.

questions.q: When Ornan met David, what did David ask of him?
questions.a: He asked Ornan to sell him the threshing floor.

questions.q: What did Ornan offer that David refused?
questions.a: He offered to give him the threshing floor, the oxen, and wheat without cost.

questions.q: After David bought the threshing floor and built an altar, how did Yahweh answer his prayer?
questions.a: Yahweh answered him with fire from heaven on the altar and told the angel to put his sword away.

questions.q: What did David do at the threshing floor of Ornan after he saw that Yahweh had answered him?
Why did David not go to the shrine of Gibeon?
questions.a: David was afraid that Yahweh’s angel might kill him.

commentary.text: —No mention is made in this book of David's sin in the matter of Uriah, neither of the troubles that followed it: they had no needful connexion with the subjects here noted. But David's sin, in numbering the people, is related: in the atonement made for that sin, there was notice of the place on which the temple should be built. The command to David to build an altar, was a blessed token of reconciliation. God testified his acceptance of David's offerings on this altar. Thus Christ was made sin, and a curse for us; it pleased the Lord to bruise him, that through him, God might be to us, not a consuming Fire, but a reconciled God. It is good to continue attendance on those ordinances in which we have experienced the tokens of God's presence, and have found that he is with us of a truth. Here God graciously met me, therefore I will still expect to meet him.
